answer: Make every agent write its work in ink: each job leaves a signed entry in a public journal, written with the agent's own quill so a thousand clones cannot hide behind one shared script, because their journals would read word for word alike. Each agent also carries a pigment, a stylistic fingerprint, and peers learn to spot the same hand behind many names. Pay goes into a vault, not a pocket: earnings stay locked until a random sample of the journal passes peer review, and copied or empty entries forfeit the lock. A sybil farm can copy text, but it cannot copy a lived record.
